transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
Pope Leo is adding his voice to the rising concern over the rapid introduction of artificial
intelligence.
Speaking at the UNESCO Headquarters in Paris Friday, the pontiff said the fears are real.
Without a shared ethical foundation, the many channels of communication risk multiplying
false information and giving currency to words devoid of meaning, thereby hindering dialogue
rather than fostering it.
artificial intelligence amplifies this problem.
Leo said he welcomes an initiative by UNESCO to promote the responsible use of media and
digital tools, including AI.
A major storm is hitting the mid-Atlantic region of the U.S. at this hour, bringing
winds and rain along with massive waves in some areas.
Millions of people are facing storm warnings, and power has been lost in thousands of homes
so far.
The Red Sox have already made adjustments to their schedule because of the weather, and
Cape Cod is expecting winds as high as 65 miles an hour.
President Trump is expected to attend Saturday's Tennessee Texas football game in Knoxville
as Jackie Seabro, member station WUOT, reports the visit is stirring mixed reaction from
students.
Trump's presence comes as the University of Tennessee's campus is already teeming
with activity for ESPN's College Game Day show.
And Cooper Dabbs participated in festivities hosted by ESPN.
"This is going to be a great environment.
I think we have a good shot at winning if the fans help out."
Student Amber Henderson looks forward to the game, but has reservations.
"I don't think that the game is about football anymore.
I think it's more so about politics."
Fans are expected to see heightened security as they enter the stadium.
For NPR News, I'm Jackie Seabro in Knoxville.
An appeals court heard arguments Friday on whether to bring back to the U.S. more than
a hundred people deported to Venezuela last year.
NPR's Nate Perez has our report.
The Venezuelans were deported under the Alien Enemies Act, a rarely used policy previously
reserved for wartime.
They were sent to El Salvador's infamous prison, Secote, despite a court ordering the
return of their flight.
Lawyers for the deported men said the U.S. government violated their due process rights
as most of the plaintiffs were in immigration proceedings prior to being detained.
But some on the three-judge panel were skeptical whether this appeals court is capable of determining
whether the deported men could challenge their imprisonment in a foreign country.
The case could be decided by next week.
Nate Perez, NPR News.
The Supreme Court Friday rejected efforts by Republicans in Missouri to use a redistricting
map backed by President Trump.
It was the third time the high court has ruled against the plan.
Republicans had drawn the new map in an effort to gain one more red seat in the House of
Representatives.
The court said using the new map could lead to electoral chaos.
You're listening to NPR News.
A federal judge in Oklahoma handed a win to a Jewish charter school this week.
State Impact Oklahoma's Beth Wallace reports this would be the nation's first publicly
funded religious school.
Earlier this year, a state board rejected the application for Ben Gamla Jewish Charter
School, a virtual school providing religious education.
The board relied on a 2024 Oklahoma Supreme Court ruling for a similar case with a Catholic
school.
Now a judge says that rejection was discriminatory.
Rachel Lazar is the president of Americans United for Separation of Church and State,
which has joined the case.
We're directly funding with taxpayer money, religious education, and turning government
schools into religious government schools.
If appealed, the case could wind up before the U.S. Supreme Court, which was split on
a similar case last year.
For NPR News, I'm Beth Wallace in Tulsa.
Former Heisman Trophy winner Tim Tebow says he's temporarily ended his relationship with
the Christian group Life Surge.
The organization has been accused of using predatory sales tactics to exploit its followers'
financial insecurity.
Tebow has earned tens of thousands of dollars offering talks at Life Surge events.
He says his team is conducting an investigation into the claims.
Fighting has begun again between federal troops and rebels in the Ethiopian city of Tigray.
Many civilians are trying to escape the fighting by moving to other provinces.
The renewed fighting has ended a 2022 peace agreement that ended a two-year war in Tigray.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Pope Francis expresses concerns about rapid artificial intelligence introduction at UNESCO Paris headquarters
Major storm hits mid-Atlantic region with high winds, rain, and power outages affecting thousands
President Trump expected to attend Tennessee-Texas football game Saturday in Knoxville amid mixed student reactions
Appeals court hears arguments on returning over hundred Venezuelans deported to El Salvador last year
Supreme Court rejects Republican redistricting map backed by President Trump in Missouri case
Federal judge rules Oklahoma rejection of Jewish charter school application was discriminatory
Former Heisman Trophy winner Tim Tebow ends relationship with Christian group Life Surge under investigation
Fighting resumes between federal troops and rebels in Ethiopian city of Tigray after 2022 peace agreement
